formats.key: Order(uint256 nonceAndMeta,uint128 expiry,address makerAsset,address takerAsset,address maker,address taker,uint256 makerAmount,uint256 takerAmount)
effects: The signer (maker) lets the allowed taker pull up to makerAmount of makerAsset from the signer's wallet (_fillOrder: transferTokens(order.makerAsset, maker, target, makerTokenFillAmount)).
The maker asset goes to a `target` address that the filler picks (fillOrderWithTarget / partialFillOrderWithTarget), not necessarily the taker.
The signer receives takerAsset from the filler, up to takerAmount, at the signer's own address (transferTokens(order.takerAsset, msg.sender, maker, takerTokenFillAmount)).
The order can be filled in several parts at the signed rate (partialFillOrder*, tryBatchFill*); each part gives makerAmount*fill/takerAmount.
If taker is the zero address, anyone can fill the order (_checkOrder: taker == address(0) || taker == msg.sender).
If expiry is 0, the order never expires; it stays valid until it is filled or the signer calls cancelOrder (_checkOrder: expiry == 0 || block.timestamp <= expiry).
formats.shown: "AugustusRFQ ERC20 order" with a raw nonce, the expiry date (hidden when 0), the maker and taker tokens by name, raw maker and taker addresses, and the maker and taker amounts formatted with their tokens.

findings.title: Order intent "AugustusRFQ ERC20 order" does not say the signer sells makerAsset for takerAsset.
findings.evidence: descriptor.json Order intent "AugustusRFQ ERC20 order", no interpolatedIntent; AugustusRFQ.sol _fillOrder moves makerAsset out of the maker and takerAsset in. Case 0 screen gives no direction for 3000 USDC vs 1 WETH.
findings.fix: Use intent "Sign swap order" and interpolatedIntent "Sell {makerAmount} for {takerAmount}".

findings.title: Order labels Maker/Taker amount do not tell the signer which amount they give and which they get.
findings.evidence: descriptor.json labels 'Maker asset', 'Taker asset', 'Maker amount', 'Taker amount'. The signer of the EIP-712 message is `maker` (_checkOrder: SignatureChecker.isValidSignatureNow(maker, ...)), so makerAmount is what leaves the signer and takerAmount is what arrives.
findings.fix: Relabel to 'You send' / 'Token you send' and 'You receive' / 'Token you receive'.

findings.title: Order hides expiry 0, so the signer is not told that the order never expires.
findings.evidence: descriptor.json expiry visible {ifNotIn:[0,'0']}; AugustusRFQ.sol _checkOrder `require(expiry == 0 || block.timestamp <= expiry)`. In case 1 the screen has no expiry field at all.
findings.fix: Show the expiry always, and render 0 as 'Never' (with a message, or a separate field visible only when expiry is 0).

findings.title: Order shows maker/taker as raw hex, and taker 0x0 is not explained as 'anyone can fill'.
findings.evidence: descriptor.json maker/taker format 'raw'; case 1 shows 'Taker address' 0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000000; _checkOrder `taker == address(0) || taker == msg.sender`.
findings.fix: Use addressName for both; label taker 'Allowed counterparty' and say that the zero address means anyone.

findings.title: Order amounts are totals; partial fills at the signed rate are allowed and not mentioned.
findings.evidence: AugustusRFQ.sol partialFillOrderWithTarget: makerTokenFilledAmount = takerTokenFillAmount * makerAmount / takerAmount; _checkOrder tracks remaining.

findings.title: Order shows nonceAndMeta as a raw integer that means nothing to the signer.
findings.evidence: descriptor.json nonceAndMeta format 'raw'; the struct comment says 'Nonce and taker specific metadata'; it only makes the order hash unique.
findings.fix: Hide it or label it 'Order nonce'.

formats.key: OrderNFT(uint256 nonceAndMeta,uint128 expiry,uint256 makerAsset,uint256 makerAssetId,uint256 takerAsset,uint256 takerAssetId,address maker,address taker,uint256 makerAmount,uint256 takerAmount)
effects: The signer (maker) lets the allowed taker pull makerAmount of the maker asset (ERC20, ERC1155 id makerAssetId, or ERC721 id makerAssetId, chosen by bits 160-161 of makerAsset) from the signer's wallet to a `target` the filler picks (transferTokensNFT).
The signer receives takerAmount of the taker asset (ERC20/ERC1155/ERC721 by its packed type, with takerAssetId) from the filler, at the signer's own address.
Partial fills are possible at the signed rate (partialFillOrderNFT, batchFillOrderWithTargetNFT).
If taker is the zero address, anyone can fill the order.
If expiry is 0, the order never expires; it stays valid until it is filled or the signer cancels it.
formats.shown: "AugustusRFQ NFT order" with every value raw: the nonce, the packed asset integers, the NFT ids, hex addresses and unscaled amounts; the expiry is shown as a date only when it is not 0.

findings.title: OrderNFT shows maker/taker assets as raw packed uint256, so the token and its type cannot be read.
findings.evidence: descriptor.json makerAsset/takerAsset format 'raw' ('Maker asset encoded'); AugustusRFQ.sol comment '0 - 159 bits are address, 160 - 161 bits are tokenType'. Case 2 shows makerAsset 2536500777716045908446414720245124845575819686205 (type 1, 0xBC4CA0…f13D) and takerAsset 1097077688018008265106216665536940668749033598146 (WETH).
findings.fix: Show `makerAsset.[-20:]` and `takerAsset.[-20:]` with addressName (types token, collection), and the type byte `makerAsset.[11:12]` with an enum: 0 ERC20, 1 ERC1155, 2 ERC721.

findings.title: OrderNFT shows makerAmount/takerAmount raw; case 2 shows 15 WETH as 15000000000000000000.
findings.evidence: descriptor.json makerAmount/takerAmount format 'raw'; case 2 'Taker amount' 15000000000000000000 with WETH packed in takerAsset.
findings.fix: Use tokenAmount with tokenPath `takerAsset.[-20:]` / `makerAsset.[-20:]` (it falls back to a plain count for NFTs).

findings.title: OrderNFT intent does not say what the signer gives and what they receive.
findings.evidence: descriptor.json intent "AugustusRFQ NFT order", no interpolatedIntent; _fillOrderNFT moves makerAsset out of the maker and takerAsset in.
findings.fix: Use intent "Sign NFT swap order" and interpolatedIntent "Give {makerAmount} of {makerAsset} for {takerAmount} of {takerAsset}" (with sliced paths).

findings.title: OrderNFT Maker/Taker labels and raw hex addresses hide which side the signer is on.
findings.evidence: descriptor.json labels 'Maker amount', 'Taker amount', 'Maker address' (raw), 'Taker address' (raw). The signer is `maker` (_checkOrder signature check), and taker 0x0 means anyone can fill.
findings.fix: Relabel to 'You send' / 'You receive'; use addressName for the addresses; say that taker 0x0 means anyone.

findings.title: OrderNFT hides expiry 0, so the signer is not told that the order never expires.
findings.evidence: descriptor.json expiry visible {ifNotIn:[0,'0']}; _checkOrder `expiry == 0 || block.timestamp <= expiry`. Case 3 has no expiry field.
findings.fix: Show the expiry always and render 0 as 'Never'.

findings.title: OrderNFT shows asset IDs even for ERC20 sides, where the contract ignores them.
findings.evidence: AugustusRFQ.sol struct comment 'simply ignored in case of ERC20s'; case 2 shows 'Taker asset NFT ID: 0' for WETH.

findings.title: OrderNFT cases 2/3 pack BAYC (an ERC721) as token type 1 (ERC1155), which would revert when filled.
findings.evidence: cases/2.json and 3.json makerAsset 2536500777716045908446414720245124845575819686205 = 2^160 + 0xBC4CA0EdA7647A8aB7C2061c2E118A18a936f13D; transferTokensNFT tokenType 1 calls IERC1155.safeTransferFrom.
findings.fix: Use type 2 (2*2^160 + address) for an ERC721 collection in the test cases.

findings.title: OrderNFT shows nonceAndMeta as a raw integer that means nothing to the signer.
findings.fix: Hide it or label it 'Order nonce'.
